answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing, each measured. (1) akienasus 2026-11-12: /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns read 1, and `cairn test --exec` refused because bwrap could not build the seal (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py:247 reads that key). (2) akiendelllinux reads 0 from /etc/sysctl.d/60-uu-userns.conf, a UU-era file that nothing in either repo installs. (3) After applying the same file on akienasus, test_deposit is green and `bin/cairn test --exec true --timeout 30` exits 0.
answers.builder_check: A builder on a bare box needs only the node's apply block (sudo tee the file, sysctl -p, apt-get install bubblewrap) and its verify command, both written out in full in the intention.

answers.collision_check: The tester's isolation.py already names the fix in its refusal text ('fix: sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0'), which is live-only and is lost at reboot. This node persists it, so it is a distinction, not a collision. The cost (a wider unprivileged attack surface, the kernel's pre-24.04 default) is recorded in the node and matches the Dell since UU.
